rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording has fronting and postponement: God is praised for a book made upright, with no crookedness.
rows.anchor: فيه تقديم وتأخير وتقديره الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qayyiman means balanced, straight, even, and free of contradiction.
rows.anchor: وعنى بقوله قيما معتدلا مستقيما مستويا لا تناقض فيه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Qayyiman describes the Qur'an as guardian over earlier scriptures: it confirms and preserves them, rejects falsehood, and abrogates their laws.
rows.anchor: قيما على سائر الكتب المتقدمة يصدقها ويحفظها وينفي البطل عنها وهو ناسخ لشرائعها عن الفراء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Qayyiman means the Qur'an governs religious matters and is their reference, like a household steward.
rows.anchor: قيما لأمور الدين يلزم الرجوع إليه فيها كقيم الدار الذي يرجع إليه في أمرها عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Qayyiman means enduring and firm until the Resurrection, without being abrogated.
rows.anchor: قيما دائما يدوم ويثبت إلى يوم القيامة لا ينسخ عن الأصم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The book has no ambiguity or crookedness and is not difficult to understand.
rows.anchor: لم يجعله ملتبسا لا يفهم ومعوجا لا يستقيم وهو معنى قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The book contains no disagreement, as shown by the claim that a nondivine book would contain much disagreement.
rows.anchor: وقيل لم يجعل فيه اختلافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crookedness in speech is departure from soundness to corruption, truth to falsehood, or usefulness to futility.
rows.anchor: أن يخرج من الصحة إلى الفساد ومن الحق إلى الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is sent to make its bearer warn people of severe punishment and divine power if they do not believe.
rows.anchor: ليخوف العبد الذي أنزل عليه الكتاب الناس عذابا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who affirm God and His messenger and obey after believing receive a good reward in the Hereafter: Paradise.
rows.anchor: المصدقين بالله ورسوله الذين يعملون الطاعات بعد الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients remain in that reward forever and never leave it.
rows.anchor: لابثين في ذلك الثواب خالدين مؤبدين لا ينتقلون عنه

rows.speaker: الحسن ومحمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: The claim that God took a child refers to Quraysh's claim that the angels are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: الملائكة بنات الله وهم قريش عن الحسن ومحمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي
rows.claim: The claimants may instead be Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: هم اليهود والنصارى عن السدي والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first warning addresses unbelievers generally; this verse singles out claimants who imitate ancestors, persist in ignorance, fail to reflect, and mislead others.
rows.anchor: فعم جميع الكفار بالإنذار في الآية الأولى وخص في هذه الآية القائلين بهذه المقالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimants and their forebears have no knowledge supporting their assertion and repeat it from ignorance and imitation.
rows.anchor: ليس لهؤلاء القائلين بهذا القول الشنيع علم به ولا لأسلافهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the claimants and their fathers have no knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم بالله من علم ولا لآبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the word as coming from mouths is figurative: words are accidents, yet can be retained, written, or recited elsewhere; mentioning mouths emphasizes their declaration.
rows.anchor: ووصف الكلمة بالخروج من الأفواه توسعا ومجازا وإن كانت الكلمة عرضا لا يجوز عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have plainly voiced an enormously abhorrent statement.
rows.anchor: المعنى أنهم صرحوا بهذه الكلمة العظيمة في القبح وأظهروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement about God is nothing but a lie and fabrication.
rows.anchor: ما يقول هؤلاء إلا كذبا وافتراء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bākhiʿ means one who destroys or kills himself; Muhammad is warned against doing so over his people's rejection of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي مهلك وقاتل نفسك على آثار قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on whose traces he grieves demanded a spring from the earth before believing, in rebellion against God.
rows.anchor: الذين قالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا تمردا منهم على ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asafan means sorrow, longing, and grief over their turning away and rejecting the message.
rows.anchor: حزنا وتلهفا ووجدا بإدبارهم عنك وإعراضهم عن قبول ما آتيتهم به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On their traces can mean after their deaths, expressing the Prophet's intense compassion for them.
rows.anchor: على آثارهم أي بعد موتهم لشدة شفقتك عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On their traces can instead mean after their turning away from him.
rows.anchor: معناه من بعد توليهم وإعراضهم عنك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Asafan can mean anger and rage rather than sorrow.
rows.anchor: أسفا أي غيظا وغضبا عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is divine reproach of the Prophet for grief and eagerness for his people's faith so intense that it nearly brought him to ruin.
rows.anchor: وهذه معاتبة من الله سبحانه لرسوله على شدة وجده وكثرة حرصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿīd is the earth's surface; al-Zajjāj also glosses it as a plantless road. Juruz is barren land, imagined to consume plants.
rows.anchor: الصعيد ظهر الأرض وقال الزجاج الصعيد الطريق الذي لا نبات به والجرز الأرض التي لا تنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic describes land as jaraz or ajrāz and a drought year as al-jazar; a rajaz line witnesses the term.
rows.anchor: ويقال للسنة المجدبة الجزر لجدوبها ويبسها وقلة أمطارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as the subject because it is an interrogative with initial position; the testing clause suspends the verb in the sense of knowing which person acts best.
rows.anchor: أيهم مرفوع بالابتداء لأن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام والاستفهام له صدر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's adornment includes rivers, trees, and kinds of created things: inanimate, animal, and plant life.
rows.anchor: من الأنهار والأشجار وأنواع المخلوقات من الجماد والحيوان والنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people to expose who acts best, meaning most productively in obedience and most obedient to Him.
rows.anchor: الأحسن عملا الأعمل بطاعة الله والأطوع له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Testing means commands and prohibitions through which the obedient and disobedient become evident.
rows.anchor: معنى الابتلاء الأمر والنهي لأن بهما يظهر المطيع من العاصي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The adornment of the earth may mean its men, or its prophets and scholars.
rows.anchor: أراد بالزينة الرجال لأنهم زينة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will ruin the inhabited earth and leave its surface level, dry, and without vegetation.
rows.anchor: وإنا مخربون الأرض بعد عمارتها وجاعلون ما عليها مستويا من الأرض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The barren surface may be understood as open, desolate plains.
rows.anchor: وقيل بلاقع عن مجاهد وفي قوله أيهم أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies God wills righteous action and human acts originate from people; otherwise testing would be invalid, refuting the determinists.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله أيهم أحسن عملا دلالة على أنه سبحانه أراد من الخلق العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is understood as bal, meaning Rather, did you think the Companions of the Cave and al-Raqīm were among God's wonders?
rows.anchor: معناه بل أحسبت يا محمد

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth is more wondrous than the Cave Companions' story.
rows.anchor: فلخلق السماوات والأرض أعجب من هذا عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possibly, after the answer about the story was delayed, God asks whether this was thought extraordinary, addressing the Prophet's hope that the account would convert his questioners.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه لما استبطأ الجواب حين سألوه عن القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave is a mountain shelter where the youths took refuge.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكهف الجبل الذي أوى إليه القوم الذين قص الله أخبارهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm is the name of the valley containing the cave.
rows.anchor: اسم الوادي الذي كان فيه الكهف عن ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm is the mountain itself; the cave is a cavern in it.
rows.anchor: الكهف غار في الجبل والرقيم الجبل نفسه عن الحسن

rows.speaker: كعب والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm is the village from which the Cave Companions departed.
rows.anchor: القرية التي خرج منها أصحاب الكهف عن كعب والسدي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm is a stone tablet recording the Companions' story, placed at the cave entrance; al-Balkhī and al-Jubbāʾī prefer this account.
rows.anchor: هو لوح من حجارة كتبوا فيه قصة أصحاب الكهف ثم وضعوه على باب الكهف عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The tablet was placed among kings' treasuries because it was extraordinary.
rows.anchor: جعل ذلك اللوح في خزائن الملوك لأنه من عجائب الأمور

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm is a book whose contents God did not disclose.
rows.anchor: الرقيم كتاب ولذلك الكتاب خبر فلم يخبرالله تعالى عما فيه عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
rows.claim: The Companions of al-Raqīm may be three men trapped when a rock sealed their cave; each invoked God by a good deed, and the Prophet reported their rescue.
rows.anchor: إن أصحاب الرقيم هم النفر الثلاثة الذين دخلوا في غار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn means abiding residence; the root is used of settling in a place.
rows.anchor: العدن الإقامة يقال عدن بالمكان يعدن عدنا

rows.speaker: قطرب وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Asāwir is a plural of aswār with an added element removed; its underlying form is asāwīr.
rows.anchor: الأساور جمع أسوار على حذف الزيادة لأن الأصل أساوير عن قطرب وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, asāwir is the plural of aswira, itself a plural of siwār, a bracelet worn on the hand.
rows.anchor: جمع سوار عن الزجاج وهو سوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk and istabraq thick silk; al-Muraqqish's verse illustrates istabraq garments.
rows.anchor: والسندس ما رق من الديباج واحده سندسة والاستبرق الغليظ من الديباج

rows.speaker: المرقش
rows.claim: Al-Muraqqish's verse uses istabraq for a silk garment.
rows.anchor: وإستبرق الديباج طورا لباسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾik is the plural of arīka, a bed; al-Zajjāj explains the furnishings as couches within canopies.
rows.anchor: والأرائك جمع أريكة وهي السرير

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses arīka for one of the couches or beds.
rows.anchor: بين الرواق وجانب من سترها منها وبين أريكة الأنضاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inna clause has three analyses: the no-waste assertion is predicate with an omitted qualifier; the Gardens may be predicate with an intervening parenthesis; or the assertion may explain the believers' reward.
rows.anchor: قيل في خبر إن الذين آمنوا أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully repays believers' obedience and does not let good deeds go to waste or reduce their reward.
rows.anchor: لا نترك أعمالهم تذهب ضياعا بل نجازيهم ونوفيهم أجورهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Adn may name the middle of Paradise; it is pluralized because it is vast and every region can serve as a garden.
rows.anchor: عدن بطنان الجنة أي وسطها وهي جنة من الجنان عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers flow beneath people because they occupy upper chambers; alternatively, Paradise's rivers run in underground channels.
rows.anchor: لأنهم على غرف في الجنة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Each person may wear three bracelets: one silver, one gold, and one pearl and ruby.
rows.anchor: إنه يحلى كل واحد بثلاثة أساور سوار من فضة وسوار من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istabraq may be a Persian loanword; another explanation calls it silk woven with gold.
rows.anchor: إن الإستبرق فارسي معرب أصله استبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reclining conveys secure comfort, since people recline only when safe; the couches are a pleasant resting or gathering place.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان لا يتكىء إلا في حال الأمن والسلامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The reward is good and great.
rows.anchor: طاب ثوابهم وعظم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم ويعقوب وسهل
rows.claim: These readers pronounce thamar with fatḥa in both occurrences; Ruways agrees in the first.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم ويعقوب وسهل وكان له ثمر وأحيط بثمره في الموضعين بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads thumr with ḍamma and a still middle consonant in both places; the remaining readers use ḍamma on both consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء وسكون الميم في الموضعين

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز وابن عامر
rows.claim: The Ḥijāz and Ibn ʿĀmir add mīm in khayran minhumā, as in their codices; Iraqi readers omit it.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز وابن عامر خيرا منهما بزيادة ميم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Thamara is what is picked from a fruit-bearing tree; its plurals include thamarāt, thamar, and thimār by analogy with other forms.
rows.anchor: الثمرة ما يجتنى من ذي الثمر وجمعها ثمرات

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr's thumr may be shortened thimār, a collective plural, or a singular; any analysis allows a quiescent middle consonant.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبي عمرو وكان له ثمر يجوز أن يكون جمع ثمار كما يخفف كتب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some linguists distinguish thamar as wealth from thumr as edible fruit; exegetes similarly take the word for palms and trees, not their fruit.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة الثمر المال والثمر المأكول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference may be fruit-bearing trees rather than fruit: expenditure was on productive roots, and the affliction uprooted them.
rows.anchor: بل الأصول التي تحمل الثمرة لا نفس الثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's greenery was erased by the calamity, becoming like a black night or white day.
rows.anchor: وما بطل من خضرتها بالآفة النازلة بها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Thumr can mean kinds of wealth; destruction of that wealth includes crops. This makes the readings with thumr clearer than fatḥa, though fatḥa may report only part of the loss.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو ثمر والثمر أنواع المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minhā is singular because it is nearer to the singular garden just mentioned; minhumā is dual because the two gardens had been mentioned.
rows.anchor: فالإفراد لأنه أقرب إلى الجنة المفردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarafa's verse illustrates ḥafāf for the sides enclosing a winged object.
rows.anchor: كأن جناحي مضرحي تكنفا حفافيه شكا في العسيب بمسرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāwarah means reciprocal speech; it is also said someone gave no response or reply.
rows.anchor: والمحاورة مراجعة الكلام في المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden story is a parable directing servants to obedience and warning them away from disobedience and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: ثم ضرب الله لعباده مثلا يستفيئهم به إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The two men were sons of an Israelite king who divided a great inheritance; the believer used his share to draw near to God, while the other bought estates including the gardens.
rows.anchor: يريد ابني ملك كان في بني إسرائيل توفي وترك ابنين وترك مالا جزيلا

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: The parable is about a rich man with two large gardens and a poor neighbor; the author says this better fits the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم أنه يريد رجلا كان له بستانان كبيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palms encircle grape gardens, and a field between them completes provision of grapes, dates, and grain.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا بين البستانين مزرعة فكملت النعمة بالعنب والتمر والزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each garden yielded its full harvest without shortfall; the crop is called food because it is eaten.
rows.anchor: كل واحدة من البستانين آتت غلتها وأخرجت ثمرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop was not diminished; a poetic line illustrates being wronged or deprived of one's property.
rows.anchor: لم تنقص منه شيئا بل أدته على التمام والكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause uses singular verb agreement with kullatā because the dual word is grammatically singular; the author cites a poem using dual agreement by sense.
rows.anchor: إنما قال أتت على لفظ كلتا فإنه بمنزلة كل في أنه مفرد اللفظ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One explanation is that the palm trees bore fruit; another is that the man owned fruit independently of the gardens.
rows.anchor: وكان للنخل الذي فيهما ثمر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The man's other wealth alongside the gardens was gold and silver.
rows.anchor: كان لهذا الرجل مع هذين البستانين الذهب والفضة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس
rows.claim: The man's other wealth consisted of all kinds of property.
rows.anchor: كان له معهما جميع الأموال عن قتادة وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving garden owner says he has more wealth and greater standing; nafar names a clan because they accompany him on errands.
rows.anchor: أي أعز عشيرة ورهطا وسمى العشيرة نفرا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Aʿaz nafaran may instead mean more servants and children.
rows.anchor: معناه أعز خدما وولدا عن قتادة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wrongs himself by entering the garden as an unbeliever and disobedient person.
rows.anchor: أي ودخل الكافر بستانه وهو ظالم لنفسه بكفره وعصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His claim that the garden will never perish may refer to the garden and its fruit, or to the whole world.
rows.anchor: ما أقدر أن تفني هذه الجنة وهذه الثمار أبدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he thinks the whole world will never perish.
rows.anchor: يريد ما أظن هذه الدنيا تفنى أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denies that the Resurrection will occur, contrary to what monotheists teach.
rows.anchor: وما أحسب القيامة آتية كائنة على ما يقوله الموحدون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The believer had told him of resurrection; the fool assumes his wealth means God favors him and will give him better after death.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن صاحبه المؤمن قد أعلمه أن الساعة تقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His boast assumes resurrection is true and claims he would find a better garden than this one.
rows.anchor: لأجدن خيرا من هذه الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he imagines earning a better return in the Hereafter than in this world.
rows.anchor: لأكتسبن في الآخرة خيرا من هذه التي اكتسبتها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shows he was not certain there is no return; he doubted the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لم يكن قاطعا على نفي المعاد بل كان شاكا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā shāʾa Allāh may mean the affair is what God wills, that whatever God wills will occur, or a conditional with an omitted answer.
rows.anchor: ما شاء الله يحتمل أن يكون ما رفعا وتقديره الأمر ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: In in tarani anā aqalla, aqalla is the second object of tarā; anā can be emphasis, apposition, or a separative pronoun.
rows.anchor: أقل منصوب بأنه مفعول ثان لترن وأنا إن شئت كان توكيدا

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: He reads aqallu in the nominative, making anā the subject and aqallu its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ بها عيسى بن عمر فيكون أنا مبتدأ وأقل خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ʿasā answers the conditional; thawāban and ʿaqban are accusatives of specification.
rows.anchor: الفاء جواب قوله أن ترني وثوابا وعقابا منصوبان على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer rebukes disbelief in the Creator, who made the interlocutor's father Adam from dust.
rows.anchor: يعني أصل الخلقة أي خلق أباك من تراب وهو آدم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Because food grows from soil and produces the fluid by which people are ordinarily created, creation from dust is apt language.
rows.anchor: لما كانت النطفة خلقها الله سبحانه بمجرى العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God moved him from state to state until making him a human being with balanced form and stature.
rows.anchor: نقلك من حال إلى حال حتى جعلك بشرا معتدل الخلقة والقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner's disbelief consisted in denying resurrection; the passage treats doubt about resurrection as unbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن الشك في البعث والنشور كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakkinnā means But I say: He is God, my Lord, creator and provider; the believer's pride is monotheism, not worldly property.
rows.anchor: تقديره لكن أنا أقول هو الله ربي وخالقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship cannot rightly be shared because it is due for foundational blessings no other benefactor can match; only God can bestow them.
rows.anchor: لا تستحق إلا بأصول النعم التي لا يوازنها نعمة منعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner had no group to shield him from God's punishment and could not defend himself.
rows.anchor: أي لم يكن لهذا الكافر جماعة يدفعون عذاب الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiah may mean a military troop; the author cites al-ʿAjjāj as linguistic evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفئة الجند قال العجاج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He could not defend himself; Ibn ʿAbbās instead says muntasiran means unable to recover what was lost.
rows.anchor: وما كان ممتنعا عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muntasiran may mean that he could not recover what he had lost.
rows.anchor: وما كان مستردا بدل ما ذهب قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men in the garden parable are identified with the companion in Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt.
rows.anchor: وهذان الرجلان هما اللذان ذكرهما الله تعالى في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report through Hishām ibn Sālim and Abān ibn ʿUthmān counsels refuge in God's words for fear, grief, plots, and worldly desire; God answers each appeal, and His promised better provision is certain.
rows.anchor: روى هشام بن سالم وأبان بن عثمان عن الصادق ع قال عجبت لمن خاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time God alone has protective authority, managing believers' affairs and granting victory to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: فهو الذي يتولى أمر عباده المؤمنين ويملك النصرة لمن أراد

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Henālik may point to the Resurrection, when people turn to God, believe in Him, and renounce what they worshipped.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى يوم القيامة وتقديره الولاية يوم القيامة لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God supports believers and humiliates unbelievers, with victory belonging exclusively to Him.
rows.anchor: معناه هنالك ينصر المؤمنين ويخذل الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the best reward and consequence; the comparison supposes another could reward, and ʿuqbā abbreviates an understood phrase about obedience's result.
rows.anchor: هو أفضل ثوابا ممن يرجى ثوابا على تقدير لو كان يثيب غيره

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the verb passive and place the mountains in the nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ويوم تسير بضم التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the active first-person verb with the mountains in the accusative, matching the following We gathered.
rows.anchor: والباقون نسير بالنون وكسر الياء والجبال نصب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The passive reading is supported by the Qur'anic passive constructions cited after his statement.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي حجة من بنى الفعل للمفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashīm is crushed dry vegetation; dhar means windblown scattering of light things, and related verbs describe throwing a rider from a mount.
rows.anchor: الهشيم ما يكسر ويحطم من يبس النبات والذر والتذرية تطيير الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mughādarah means leaving something behind, as in treachery for abandoning a pledge and a pool where water remains.
rows.anchor: ومنه الغدر لأن ترك الوفاء ومنه الغدير لترك الماء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishfāq is fear of possible harm and originally connotes tenderness; shafaq also names the sky's thin reddish dusk.
rows.anchor: الإشفاق الخوف من وقوع مكروه مع تجويز أن لا يقع وأصله الرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaffan is a circumstantial accusative meaning lined up.
rows.anchor: صفا نصب على الحال أي مصفوفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rain-fed plant grows intertwined, fresh and attractive, then becomes fragments scattered by wind, like worldly life that passes away.
rows.anchor: فانقلاب الدنيا كانقلاب هذا النبات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God had power over everything before it came into existence.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: أي كان الله مقتدرا على كل شيء قبل كونه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Following Sībawayh, al-Zajjāj says God's power did not newly arise when these signs appeared; He has always been capable.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وتأويله أن ما شاهدتم من قدرته ليس بحادث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the past-tense statement reports past power to point to future events; the parable warns wealthy braggarts who shun poor believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه إخبار عن الماضي ودلالة على المستقبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt are acts of obedience and all good deeds, whose reward lasts forever.
rows.anchor: وهي الطاعات لله تعالى وجميع الحسنات لأن ثوابها يبقى أبدا عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt may mean the four remembrances recited by poor Muslims such as Salmān and Ṣuhayb.
rows.anchor: إن الباقيات الصالحات هي ما كان يأتي به سلمان وصهيب

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: This explanation of the enduring deeds as four remembrances is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās via ʿAṭāʾ and also from Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في رواية عطاء ومجاهد وعكرمة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the four remembrances a shield from Hell, describing them as provisions, responses, sequels, and enduring good deeds.
rows.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says those unable to endure night vigil or fight should persist in the four remembrances, which are enduring good deeds.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومسروق والنخعي
rows.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt may mean the five daily prayers; this is also reported from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: هي الصلوات الخمس عن ابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومسروق والنخعي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh is also reported to identify the enduring good deeds as night prayer.
rows.anchor: أن من الباقيات الصالحات القيام باليل لصلاة الليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies enduring good deeds as righteous daughters.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الباقيات الصالحات هن البنات الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the general sense, encompassing every act of obedience and good deed.
rows.anchor: والأولى حملها على العموم فيدخل فيها جميع الطاعات والخيرات

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In Ibn ʿUqda's book, Abū ʿAbd Allāh tells al-Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān not to deem their love small, since it is among the enduring good deeds.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عقدة أن أبا عبد الله ع قال للحصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds are called righteous because God commanded them, promised reward, and threatened punishment for leaving them.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت الطاعات صالحات لأنها أصلح الأعمال للمكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may continue the preceding sentence, making enduring deeds the best reward on that day; alternatively, it begins a new command to remember the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه يتعلق بما قبله وتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God uproots and disperses the mountains; another view has them move like clouds before becoming loose sand.
rows.anchor: تسيير الجبال قلعها عن أماكنها فإن الله سبحانه يقلعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are ultimately made into mirage, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: ثم يصيرها بمنزلة السراب كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is bare, with nothing on it to screen it from view.
rows.anchor: أي ظاهرة ليس عليها شيء من جبل أو بناء أو شجر

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Alternatively, the earth's interior appears as those inside it emerge onto its surface.
rows.anchor: معناه وترى باطن الأرض ظاهرا قد برز

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying is cited to illustrate what the earth will bring forth.
rows.anchor: فهو قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is raised from the graves and gathered at the assembly; no one is left behind.
rows.anchor: وبعثناهم من قبورهم وجمعناهم في الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected are presented in rows: each community in its row, row after row, or one unobstructed row.
rows.anchor: يعني المحشورين يعرضون على الله تعالى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive powerless and poor, as at their first creation, with judgment belonging to God alone.
rows.anchor: لقد جئتمونا ضعفاء فقراء عاجزين في الموضع الذي لا يملك فيه الحكم غيرنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they arrive without worldly wealth, children, or servants.
rows.anchor: معناه ليس معكم شيء مما اكتسبتموه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells ʿĀʾisha that people are resurrected barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised; each person is too preoccupied to notice others.
rows.anchor: يحشر الناس من قبورهم يوم القيامة حفاة عراة غرلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are told they once claimed God appointed no time for resurrection, recompense, and judgment.
rows.anchor: يقال لهم أيضا بل زعمتن في دار الدنيا أن الله لم يجعل لكم موعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitāb is generic plural: books or human beings' written pages are placed in their hands.
rows.anchor: ووضع الكتب فإن الكتاب اسم جنس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Alternatively, the book means the reckoning, expressed as a book because people are judged by their written deeds.
rows.anchor: معناه ووضع الحساب فعبر عن الحساب بالكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers fear the recorded evil deeds; their cry of woe expresses distress and invokes ruin upon themselves.
rows.anchor: أي خائفين مما فيه من الأعمال السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record misses no sin, small or great; the feminine endings mean a deed or act, and the distinction was explained in al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: لا يترك صغيرة من الذنوب ولا كبيرة إلا عدها وأثبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They find their deeds written and present; alternatively, they find the consequences of their deeds as if the deeds themselves were present.
rows.anchor: أي مكتوبا في الكتاب مثبتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither reduces the good person's reward nor increases a wrongdoer's punishment; this argues against punishing children who have not sinned.
rows.anchor: ولا ينقص ربك ثواب محسن ولا يزيد في عقاب مسيء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the creation clause with majestic first-person plural nūn; the other readers use tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ما أشهدناهم بالنون على التعظيم

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamzah reads the later phrase with first-person plural nūn; the others use third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ويوم نقول بالنون والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn reading connects with the preceding first-person expression; yāʾ fits a sentence break and the sense that God says to summon the partners.
rows.anchor: من قرأ نقول بالنون حمله على ما تقدم في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading is stronger because the address says summon My partners; a nūn reading would more naturally say Our partners.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقوي القراءة بالياء لأنه لو كانت بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq is departure into a harmful state; the verb is used of a date escaping its husk and a mouse leaving its hole.
rows.anchor: الفسق الخروج إلى حال تضر يقال فسقت الرطبة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah says the term was not heard in pre-Islamic poetry or reports and was used by Arabs only after the Qur'an came.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة هذه التسمية لم نسمعها في شيء من أشعار الجاهلية

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad agrees with Abū ʿUbaydah but says fisq is still a fluent, established Arabic word.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: الأمر على ما ذكره أبو عبيدة وهي كلمة فصيحة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Fasaqa ʿan amri rabbihi can mean departing from his Lord's command, like giving clothing instead of nakedness or food instead of hunger.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب فسق عن أمر ربه أي عن رد أمر ربه

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: ʿAḍud is the arm between elbow and shoulder; related forms metaphorically mean helping someone or relying on them as support.
rows.anchor: والعضد ما بين المرفق إلى الكتف وفيه خمس لغات

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Mawbiq can mean anything lying between two things, from a root meaning to perish.
rows.anchor: قال ثعلب كل شيء حال بين شيئين فهو موبق

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: The syntax of biʾsa has an implicit subject explained by badal; al-zalimīn intervenes before the specified object, Iblis's offspring.
rows.anchor: فذرية إبليس هو المخصص بالذم عن أبي علي الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Iblis recalls to arrogant people who shun the poor what their pride leads to.
rows.anchor: أن يذكر هؤلاء المتكبرين عن مجالسة الفقراء قصة إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Iblis one of the jinn supports the view that he was not an angel, since jinn are distinct from angels as humans are.
rows.anchor: من قال إن إبليس لم يكن من الملائكة استدل بهذا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view says Iblis was an angel and jinn means beings hidden from sight, or a class of angels called jinn; the author calls these readings weak.
rows.anchor: ومن قال إنه كان من الملائكة قال إن المعنى كان من الذين يستترون عن الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative angelic interpretations are weak because unqualified jinn ordinarily means the familiar species, not angels.
rows.anchor: وضعف الأولون هذين الوجهين لأن لفظ الجن إذا أطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address rebukes people for obeying Iblis and his descendants and making them allies although they are enemies.
rows.anchor: أفتتبعون أمر إبليس وأمر ذريته وتتخذونهم أولياء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Iblis's descendants are devils.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ذريته الشياطين وقال الحسن: الجن من ذريته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the jinn are among Iblis's descendants.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ذريته الشياطين وقال الحسن: الجن من ذريته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Obeying Iblis is a bad exchange for worshipping God.
rows.anchor: بئس ما استبدلوا بعبادة ربهم إذا أطاعوا إبليس عن الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The bad exchange is obedience to Satan instead of obedience to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بئس البدل طاعة الشيطان عن طاعة الرحمن عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not bring Iblis and his offspring to witness creation or enlist them to create the heavens, earth, or themselves; He needs no helpers.
rows.anchor: ما أحضرت إبليس وذريته خلق السموات والأرض ولاخلق أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misleaders are devils who lead people astray; ʿaḍud means helpers, singular here to match the verse endings.
rows.anchor: أي الشياطين الذين يضلون الناس أعوانا يعضدونني عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, people follow Satan as though he possessed secret knowledge, although God showed him no creation or how things are made.
rows.anchor: أنكم اتبعتم الشيطان كما يتبع من يكون عنده عليم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation addresses Arab polytheists: they did not witness creation and did not yet exist, so how could they claim angels are God's daughters?
rows.anchor: ما أحضرت مشركي العرب وهؤلاء الكفار خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, idolaters are told to call partners they claimed would ward off punishment; those partners will not answer or help.
rows.anchor: يريد يوم القيامة يقول الله للمشركين وعبدة الأصنام

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: The mawbiq is a deep ravine separating people of guidance from people of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم واد عميق فرق الله به سبحانه بين أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Alternatively, the mawbiq is a barrier between deities and worshippers; the author says the supposed deities are placed with unbelievers in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بين المعبودين وعبدتهم موبقا أي حاجزا عن ابن الأعرابي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Their worldly bond and friendship in unbelief becomes a cause of destruction in the Hereafter; this is also reported from Qatādah and Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه جعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا موبقا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Mawbiq can mean enmity that is itself destructive.
rows.anchor: وقيل: موبقا عداوة عن الحسن فكأنه قال عداوة مهلكة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Mawbiq is a valley of pus and blood in Hell.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك أنه قال: الموبق واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation clause connects as argument resolving the dispute about following Iblis; alternatively, it establishes God's exclusive creative power and denies partners in worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه سبحانه بين بذلك أنه المتفرد بالخلق والاختراع

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read qubulan with two ḍammas; other readers use qubulan.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة قبلا بضمتين والباقون قبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical explanation of these readings was already given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا الوجه في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāqiʿah means forceful contact; maṣrif means a place or means of turning aside.
rows.anchor: المواقعة ملابسة الشيء بشدة ومنه وقائع الحروب

rows.speaker: أبو كبير
rows.claim: Abū Kabīr's verse uses maṣrif to mean a way of escape or turning aside.
rows.anchor: قال أبو كبير: أزهير هل عن شيبة من مصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣrīf means moving a meaning through different directions; idḥāḍ means making something slip toward ruin.
rows.anchor: والتصريف تنقيل المعنى في الجهات المختلفة والإدحاض الإذهاب بالشيء إلى الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yuʾminū is an accusative verbal noun; the exception means only expectation of punishment prevented them from believing, and mā unthirū is coordinated with God's signs.
rows.anchor: أن يؤمنوا في موضع نصب والمعنى ما منع الناس من الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The criminals may be polytheists who see the fire blazing angrily at them.
rows.anchor: رأوا النار وهي تتلظى حنقا عليهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the criminals include all grave sinners.
rows.anchor: هو عام في أصحاب الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know they will enter the fire's punishment and find no place of escape.
rows.anchor: علموا أنهم داخلون فيها واقعون في عذابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives varied examples in repeated forms to prompt reflection; this was discussed in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
rows.anchor: تصريفها ترديدها من نوع واحد وأنواع مختلفة ليتفكروا فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The combative person meant by al-insān is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
rows.anchor: يريد بالإنسان النضر بن الحارث عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The combative person meant by al-insān is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: ويريد أبي بن خلف عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-insān means unbelievers generally, as the following mention of their disputing with falsehood indicates.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه وكأن الكافر يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After guidance arrives, nothing prevents belief and seeking forgiveness except a demand for earlier peoples' fate or visible punishment.
rows.anchor: معناه ما منعهم من الإيمان بعد مجيء الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They act as if demanding punishment, since they will not believe until they see it; this resembles their challenge for stones or painful torment.
rows.anchor: أنهم بامتناعهم من الإيمان بمنزلة من يطلب هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers were sent only to bring glad tidings of Paradise for obedience and warn of Hell for disobedience.
rows.anchor: لم نرسل الرسل إلى الخلق إلا مبشرين لهم بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers argue on false grounds to drive truth from its place, demanding signs to suit their whims and invalidate Muhammad's message.
rows.anchor: ويناظر الكفار دفعا عن مذاهبهم بالباطل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās applies the false disputants to mockers and plotters with followers, demanding signs to negate the Prophet's message.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد المستهزئين والمقتسمين وأتباعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mock God's signs, the Qur'an, and warnings of resurrection and Hell.
rows.anchor: أي ما تخوفوا به من البعث والنار

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads li-mahlakihim with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on lām, matching the reading in al-Naml 27:49.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم لمهلكهم بفتح الميم وكسر اللام

rows.speaker: حماد ويحيى
rows.claim: Ḥammād and Yaḥyā, transmitting from Abū Bakr, read with fatḥa on both mīm and lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حماد ويحيى عن أبي بكر بفتح الميم واللام

rows.speaker: الأعشى والبرجمي
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā and al-Barjamī, transmitting from Abū Bakr, read with a ḍamma here and a fatḥa in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعشى والبرجمي عنه ههنا بالضم وهناك بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahlak can be a verbal noun or a time, while mahlik means a time; fatḥa on both can mean destruction, with grammatical relation depending on whether halaka is transitive.
rows.anchor: من قرأ لمهلكهم فإن المهلك يجوز أن يكون مصدرا ويجوز أن يكون وقتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Tamīm dialect uses halakanī Zayd; a cited line can likewise treat hālik as a transitive verbal noun or active description.
rows.anchor: أن تميما يقول هلكني زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilka al-qurā can be a nominative subject followed by a descriptive adjective and predicate, or an object of an implicit verb explained by ahlaknāhum.
rows.anchor: تلك رفع بالابتداء والقرى صفة لها مبينة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is more unjust than someone warned by the Qur'an and proofs of divine unity who turns away.
rows.anchor: معناه ليس أحد أظلم لنفسه ممن ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting what one's hands sent ahead means forgetting sins deserving punishment; alternatively, it means neglecting them contemptuously and heedlessly.
rows.anchor: نسي المعاصي التي استحق بها العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart-covering phrase means covers prevent understanding; the deafness is figurative, as in Luqmān 31:7.
rows.anchor: أي كراهة أن يفقهوه أو لئلا يفقهوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image means it is as though coverings were on their hearts and heaviness in their ears, preventing understanding and hearing.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى كأن على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reports they will never accept guidance; this came true because they died in unbelief.
rows.anchor: أخبر سبحانه أنهم لا يؤمنون أبدا وقد خرج مخبره موافقا لخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God covers faults, forgives believers' sins, and bestows blessings and bounty on creation.
rows.anchor: وربك الساتر على عباده الغافر لذنوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God is forgiving to the persistent sinner because He gives time rather than rushing to punish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الغفور التائب ذو الرحمة للمصر بأن يمهل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God delays immediate punishment so people may repent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الغفور لا يؤاخذهم عاجلا ذو الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had God seized them for their deeds, He would hasten worldly punishment; instead, they have an appointed Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Mawʾilan means a refuge.
rows.anchor: أي ملجأ عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mawʾilan can mean a protective place or stronghold.
rows.anchor: محرزا عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Mawʾilan may mean a means of escape or deliverance, supported by poetic lines including one by al-Aʿshā.
rows.anchor: منجا ينجيهم عن أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns refer to those of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and others, destroyed for denying God's messengers and rejecting His signs.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قرى عاد وثمود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fixed a known time for their destruction, delaying it until then for a reason.
rows.anchor: أي وجعلنا لوقت إهلاكهم أو لوقت هلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says We destroyed them using a plural pronoun for residents, because the town itself does not merit destruction; its unjust inhabitants do.
rows.anchor: لأن القرية هي المسكن نحو المدينة والبلدة وهي لا تستحق الهلاك

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ pronounces the hāʾ in wa-mā ansānīhi with ḍamma; the other readers use kasra, while Ibn Kathīr retains yāʾ in liaison.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص وما أنسانيه بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā abraḥa means I keep going; interpreting it as not moving would be absurd, since Moses continued overland.
rows.anchor: لا أبرح أي لا أزال ولو كان معناه لا أزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses abraḥu to mean I continue to be or remain in a state.
rows.anchor: وأبرح ما أدام الله قومي رخي البال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ḥuqb means eighty years.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج والحقب ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarb means a path or route; its underlying sense is a tunnel through earth.
rows.anchor: والسرب المسلك والمذهب ومعناه في اللغة المحفور في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab, waṣab, and taʿab are synonyms for weakness or strain caused by toil.
rows.anchor: والنصب والوصب والتعب نظائر وهو الوهن الذي يكون على الكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarban may be a second object of ittakhadha or a cognate accusative implied by the fish taking its path.
rows.anchor: سربا منصوب على وجهين: أحدهما: أن يكون مفعولا ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adhkurahu is an accusative substitute for the pronoun in ansānīhi; ʿajaban may be Yūshaʿ's comment or Moses's amazed response.
rows.anchor: أن أذكره في موضع نصب بدل من الهاء في أنسانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣan may describe them as tracing their route or serve as a cognate accusative for following the tracks.
rows.anchor: وقصصا وضع موضع الحال تقديره يقصان الأثر قصصا

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: After the Prophet told Quraysh the Cave Companions' story, they asked about Moses's instructed learned companion and this account was revealed.
rows.anchor: ذكر علي بن إبراهيم في تفسيره قال لما أخبر رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators identify Moses as Moses son of ʿImrān; Yūshaʿ was his youth because he accompanied him while traveling and studying.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أنه موسى بن عمران وفتاه يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Yūshaʿ was called his youth because he served him, explaining the request for breakfast; his lineage is given through Joseph and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كان يخدمه ولهذا قال له آتنا غداءنا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: The People of the Book say the Moses seeking al-Khiḍr was Moses son of Mīshā son of Joseph, a prophet before Moses son of ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق يقول أهل الكتاب إن موسى الذي طلب الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's identification with Moses son of ʿImrān is preferred: an unqualified Moses means the prominent figure, as Muhammad means the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الذي عليه الجمهور أنه موسى بن عمران

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: Replying to Yūnus and Hishām ibn Ibrāhīm, al-Riḍā says Moses met the learned man on a sea island; Moses asked to learn, but the man said their assigned knowledge differed and Moses could not endure his.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي الحسن الرضا ع يسألونه عن ذلك فكتب في الجواب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The meeting point is where the Persian Sea from the east and Byzantine Sea from the west meet.
rows.anchor: ملتقى البحرين بحر فارس وبحر الروم ومما يلي المغرب

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: The meeting point is Tangier; another report from him says Africa.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب هو طنجة وروي عنه إفريقية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ḥuqb is an age or long period.
rows.anchor: أي دهرا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Ḥuqb means seventy years.
rows.anchor: سبعين سنة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ḥuqb means eighty years.
rows.anchor: ثمانين سنة عن عبد الله بن عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reached where the seas meet; they forgot the fish, or it escaped their notice when it made a tunnel through the sea.
rows.anchor: أي فلما بلغا الموضع الذي يجتمع فيه رأس البحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, only Yūshaʿ forgot, but the dual is used because he cared for provisions; or both forgot different duties about the fish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه من النسيان والناسي له كان أحدهما وهو يوشع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses and his youth carried a salted fish as provisions.
rows.anchor: تزودا حوتا مملوحا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The provision was a fresh fish rather than salted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حوتا طريا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūshaʿ's ablution water from the Spring of Life revived the fish; it leapt into the sea, whose water froze alongside its path.
rows.anchor: وعنده عين ماء تسمى عين الحياة فجلس يوشع بن نون وتوضأ من تلك العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the rest of a day and night, Moses asked for breakfast; ghidāʾ is morning food, ʿashāʾ evening food, and people need breakfast more.
rows.anchor: فلما كان من الغد قال موسى ليوشع آتنا غداءنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say God made Moses hungry so he would remember the fish.
rows.anchor: قالوا إن الله تعالى ألقى على موسى الجوع ليتذكر حديث الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūshaʿ recalls that he left or lost track of the fish at the rock; alternatively, he forgot to tell Moses what he saw.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن يوشع تذكر قصة الحوت لما دعا موسى بالطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Yūshaʿ told Moses about the fish at the rock, Moses would not have passed it or suffered that day's weariness.
rows.anchor: لو ذكر لموسى ع قصه الحوت عند الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish's remarkable path was a channel left open in the parted water.
rows.anchor: أي سبيلا عجبا وهو أن الماء انجاب عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Yūshaʿ's speech ends with the fish taking its route, and Moses responds with amazement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن كلام يوشع قد انقطع عند قوله واتخذ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another reading says Moses followed the fish's route through the sea, entered its opening, and found al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن معناه واتخذ موسى سبيل الحوت في البحر عجبا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recognizes the rock and fish as the sign they sought, then retraces the route and tracks with Yūshaʿ ahead.
rows.anchor: قال موسى ع ذلك ما كنا نطلب من العلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣan means they followed the tracks until reaching where the fish had entered.
rows.anchor: أي ويتبعانها ويوشع أمام موسى ع حتى انتهيا إلى مدخل الحوت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that Moses claimed to be most knowledgeable, was directed to a more learned servant at the sea junction, and carried the fish with Yūshaʿ until it escaped at the rock.
rows.anchor: إن موسى قام خطيبا في بني إسرائيل فسئل أي الناس أعلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report continues with Moses meeting al-Khiḍr, whose knowledge and Moses's compare with God's as water a bird takes from the sea, demonstrating the limits of human knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما علمي وعلمك من علم الله إلا مثل ما نقص هذا العصفور من هذا البحر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet concludes he wished Moses had remained patient so they could hear more of the two men's story.
rows.anchor: وددنا أن موسى كان صبر حتى يقص علينا من خبرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly recited that a king ahead seized every sound ship by force and that the boy was an unbeliever with believing parents; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit this reading.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير كان ابن عباس يقرأ وكان أمامهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة صالحة غصبا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The Imāmī authorities also report the sound-ship reading from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: وروى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله ع أيضا أنه كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The reading is also reported from Abū Jaʿfar and identified as the reading of ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك أيضا عن أبي جعفر قال وهي قراءة أمير المؤمنين ع
